The trash attributes deletions to the wrong person. There is no record of who
deleted a document, so the trash infers the deleting user from
`lastModifiedById`. That has two bad effects:

- When someone deletes a page that has nested pages, every nested page shows
  whoever last edited it, not the person who deleted the tree.
- Deleting a document rewrites the edit history: the deleter becomes the
  `lastModifiedById` of the document and all of its descendants.

Please record the deleting user properly, on the server side:

- Documents get a `deletedById` column (a nullable reference to a user).
- Soft-deleting a document records the acting user in `deletedById`. This
  includes nested documents deleted along with their parent. Restoring a
  document clears it.
- Deleting a document no longer changes `lastModifiedById` on its nested
  documents (deleting a document still records the deleter as the last
  modifier of that document itself, as it does today).
- Document API responses (for example `documents.info` and `documents.deleted`)
  include `deletedBy`, the presented user who deleted the document, for deleted
  documents. Documents that are not deleted have no `deletedBy`.
- The existing `deletedById` filter on `documents.deleted` keeps working.

The web client is out of scope.

Work within this local repository and the context you have been given. Do not
look up this project or its history online.

Verify your work before you finish: add or update automated tests that cover
the change, run them together with the existing tests for the code you touched,
and make sure they pass.

The server now records who deleted each document in a new `deletedById` column, and the trash no longer guesses from `lastModifiedById`. The tests for the code I touched pass (455 + 108), and type-checking, lint and formatting are clean.

**What changed**
- **Migration** (`server/migrations/20261019120000-add-deleted-by-id-to-documents.js`): adds a nullable `documents.deletedById` that references `users.id`. I ran it against the test database; you'll need `yarn db:migrate` in other environments.
- **Model** (`server/models/Document.ts`): new `deletedById` column and `deletedBy` association.
- **Deleting**: deleting a document records the user in `deletedById`, and so does every nested document deleted with it. It still sets `lastModifiedById` on the document itself, as before. It no longer touches `lastModifiedById` on nested documents, so their edit history stays intact.
- **Restoring** (`restoreTo`): clears `deletedById`.
- **API responses** (`server/presenters/document.ts`): deleted documents include `deletedBy` as a presented user; other documents don't have it. The user is still shown if they have since been deleted. `documents.deleted` looks up all the deleting users in one query rather than one per document.
- **Filter**: the `deletedById` filter on `documents.deleted` now uses the real column instead of mapping to `lastModifiedById`.

**One thing I added beyond the request:** deleting a whole collection soft-deletes its non-archived documents in one bulk update. That update now also sets `deletedById`, so those documents show who deleted them in the trash. It still sets `lastModifiedById` on them, as it did before. Say if you'd rather leave collection deletion alone.

**Tests**
- I rewrote the existing nested-delete test, which used to assert that the child's `lastModifiedById` became the deleter. It now asserts the child keeps its original last modifier, and that both documents get `deletedById` and appear in the filter.
- I added tests that:
  - `documents.info` includes `deletedBy` only for deleted documents;
  - restoring clears `deletedById` and `deletedBy`;
  - the model and collection delete paths record `deletedById`.
- Test files run: `documents.test.ts`, `Document.test.ts`, `Collection.test.ts`, `documentRestorer.test.ts`, the presenter tests and `collections.test.ts`.
